kind_note: Compute mode (reasoning.mode set to pro) on the GPT-5.6 Sol model, chosen from the ChatGPT model picker after Sol; not a separately shipped model
note: Lab (OpenAI) is correct. Kind 'tier' is kept, but sources describe Sol Pro as a mode of GPT-5.6 Sol, not a separate model; a third-party write-up says Sol Pro and Sol Ultra run on the same model and price. The only page I opened that dates Sol Pro is https://thegtmdirectory.com/models/openai-gpt-sol-pro/gpt-5.6-sol-pro, whose FAQ says: "GPT-5.6 Sol Pro was released on 2026-07-09 and has a knowledge cutoff of 2026-02-16." I did not record that as the tier's release: it is a third-party directory, the same page lists the status as both preview and ga, and the date is the base model's general-availability date, which the tier inherits rather than has. Base-model context, from third-party sources not opened in full: a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 family around 2026-06-26 (DataLearner), and general availability on 2026-07-09 (OpenRouter listing 'gpt-5.6-sol-20260709'; Axios URL dated 2026/07/09). OpenAI's help article (help.openai.com/en/articles/20001354-gpt-56) describes choosing Pro after GPT-5.6 Sol, but the fetch returned 403 and I saw only search snippets. Not settled: no OpenAI primary source dates the Pro mode; the OpenRouter sol-20260709 page returned 404, and the DataLearner page redirected to llmlearner.com, which I did not follow. An OpenAI release note or model-card date for the Pro mode would settle it.
